That happens against a macro this report has already documented — Brent near $99 with Gulf crude exports down 47% for 191 days, and headline CPI at 3.3% YoY. Rising fuel is a regressive tax that manufactures DG customers, and the August CPI on 09-11 is the next dated reading of it. counter_argument: The strongest case against is that DG has already made the move — +28.5% in three months and +8.4% in five sessions — so the breakout buyer is paying for the news. thesis: THE PRIMES ARE IN A BEAR MARKET DURING A SHOOTING WAR, AND THE REASON IS A FUNDING CALENDAR RATHER THAN A DEMAND PROBLEM. LMT has lost 24.1% from its 692.00 high and closed at 525.28, with NOC -33.5% and RTX -11.5%, while the US is 191 days into an air and naval campaign against Iran that has closed the Strait of Hormuz and cut Gulf crude exports by 47%. The de-rating has causes and they are real, but they are timing and idiosyncratic: production ramps are bottlenecked behind appropriations that have not cleared Congress, NOC cut its own guidance on a space-program wind-down, and the group entered 2026 on premium multiples. What has not deteriorated is LMT's own delivery. The four fetched quarterly actuals are 6.95, 7.43, 6.44 and 7.94 — beats of 8.2%, 29.0% and 10.5% against one 5.2% miss — for $28.76 of trailing EPS, putting the stock at 18.3x while the sell side revises the other way: bullish share 46.4%, up 7.1 points, strong buys 5 to 6 and holds 16 to 14. A stock falling 24% while its estimates and its ratings both improve is the shape worth owning, and the accumulation level exists because at 525 it is not yet cheap enough to clear this report's own floor.
key_risk: INVALIDATION, EXPLICITLY: two consecutive quarters of segment operating margin decline accompanied by new fixed-price program charges, or an enacted FY27 budget that cuts the baseline below $895B in real terms. Either would mean the de-rating is about earnings power rather than timing, and 18.3x becomes a value trap — this is precisely how the defense primes lost the 2010s, on fixed-price development contracts absorbing overruns the customer would not fund. Two lesser risks belong on the record: there is ZERO open-market insider buying at LMT, NOC or RTX in the last six months, which for a supposedly washed-out group is a conspicuous absence rather than a confirmation; and this idea was researched inside a compressed window, so the $28.76 trailing figure is the reported number rather than a segment-level teardown.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 18.3x trailing is not distressed — LMT traded 15-18x for most of the 2010s, so this is a normalisation from a 24x war premium rather than a discount, and the buyer at 525 is catching a knife that has fallen five sessions running into 524.03. That argument is why the entry is 495 and not 525, and why the bear case is the actual 52-week low of 437.25 (15.2x) rather than a comfortable one: from 525 the ratio is 1.45 and the idea does not publish. Below 495 it is 2.51, and the difference between those two numbers is the entire discipline here.

thesis: UPDATE TO AN OPEN POSITION — ATTACHING THE CATALYST DATE AND FIXING THE HORIZON, NOT CHANGING THE TRADE. The book is long SVRA from 5.35 (2026-08-23) targeting 8.00 with a 4.60 stop; last 5.37, +0.4%, and the only session since the last review was 2026-09-04, unchanged. What this run establishes is the thing the position was carrying without: the binary has a date, and it is 2026-11-22, not August. The FDA extended the molgramostim BLA review by three months from an original 2026-08-22 Priority Review action date because the company's own responses to information requests were deemed a major amendment — and the agency cited no safety, efficacy or manufacturing concern in doing so, which is the distinction between a procedural extension and a signal. Molgramostim carries Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations in an ultra-rare indication with no approved therapy. That makes this a 75-day hold on one agency decision, not the swing it was filed as.
key_risk: A single-asset, single-indication micro cap whose entire value resolves on one date. A complete response letter takes this well below the 4.60 stop in one gap — the stop does not protect a binary, it only defines the size of the bet, which is why the position is 1% and tiered lottery. Liquidity is the second constraint and it is real: 30-day dollar volume is about $8M, so the position must stay a small fraction of a day's trade and a bad print will not have a bid at 4.60. Dilution is the third: a company approaching a commercial launch with no approved product is the standard profile for a raise, and an offering priced into this tape would hit the stop without the FDA saying anything at all.
counter_argument: The strongest case against holding is that a three-month extension is exactly what a quiet problem looks like, and that the FDA declining to cite a concern in a press release is not the same as there being none — companies write those releases. That is fair, and it is why nothing here is added and the target is unchanged. What answers it partially is the mechanism: the amendment came from Savara's own responses to information requests rather than from an agency deficiency letter, and the review clock reset is the routine consequence of new data being submitted. The honest position is that this is a 1% lottery ticket whose thesis is a coin-weighting, not a certainty.

thesis: THE TRADE-DOWN IS NO LONGER A FORECAST — THE COMPANY MEASURED IT AND RAISED GUIDANCE ON IT. Q2 (quarter ended 2026-07-31, reported 2026-08-27) put up $2.48 diluted EPS against $2.01 expected and $1.86 a year ago, on net sales +5.2% to $11.29B and same-store sales +3.5% split 2.0% traffic and 1.5% ticket. The line that matters is non-consumables comping +4.5% explicitly on trade-down from middle- and high-income customers: DG is taking share from above, in the discretionary basket, where the margin is. Full-year EPS guidance went to $7.80-8.00 from $7.20-7.45. The tape then did something better than a gap: the print opened DG at 127.84, ran to 132.50 and FADED to close 125.89, gave the rest back to 122.89 the next session, and only then ground higher across five sessions to 133.21, taking the 200-day at 126.10 on 2026-09-01. A re-rating the market rejected on the day and accepted over the following week is post-earnings drift rather than a headline pop, which is why the trigger sits above both the 132.50 print high and the 134.12 drift high rather than chasing either. Behind it is a macro this report documented independently today — Brent near $99 with Gulf crude exports down 47% for 191 days, headline CPI 3.3% YoY, and a 96%-priced +0.3%-or-hotter August print on Friday. Rising fuel is a regressive tax that manufactures DG customers.
key_risk: About 81 basis points of the gross-margin improvement to 32.6% came from tariff refunds, worth roughly $0.25 of the EPS beat — a one-time item inside the number the market re-rated on, so the underlying margin gain is closer to 50bp than 130bp. Second, and visible in the fetched bars: the drift into resistance has come on FALLING volume — 6.4M on the print, then 3.3M, 4.2M, 3.9M, 2.8M, 1.7M, 1.7M — so the last two sessions made the highs on the thinnest tape of the month. A breakout that has to be carried by 1.7M shares is the kind that fails back into the range, which is what the 125.60 stop under the 200-day is for. Third, this is a breakout entry 15.8% below the 52-week high into a week carrying both a CPI print and an FOMC.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that DG has already made the move — +28.5% in three months and +8.4% in the five sessions since the print — so the breakout buyer is paying for news that is a week old. Two things answer it. The re-rating is arithmetically justified rather than sentimental: at 133.21 against $7.90 mid-guidance the stock is 16.9x, and the 155.00 target is 19.6x, both inside the range DG carried before its 2023-24 de-rating and below the 158.23 52-week high. And trade-down is the rare thesis that strengthens as the macro gets worse, which is the opposite exposure to everything else in this book — the SPY short, the closed TLT long and the BCC long all want Friday's CPI to go one way, and DG is the only line that wants it to go the other.
